name: Order dedup keeps the earliest event
logic: row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY order_id ORDER BY occurred_at) ... WHERE rn = 1
plain: When an order arrives more than once, the first version wins; ties on time are not broken

evidence.excerpt: SELECT *, row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY order_id ORDER BY occurred_at) rn

conflicts.note: says dedup by row_number over natural key; does not say earliest wins

meaning: Corrections to an order sent later are ignored; the first version is the one reported
impact: The Silver pipeline must reproduce 'earliest wins' or the client must approve 'latest wins'
risk: A changed tie-break silently changes revenue and order counts after cut-over

recommendation.reason: owner must say whether first or latest version is correct (OQ-08)

name: Payment dedup keeps the earliest event
logic: row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY payment_id ORDER BY occurred_at) ... WHERE rn = 1
plain: Only the first event per payment is kept, so later status changes (e.g. refund) never reach Silver

evidence.excerpt: SELECT *, row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY payment_id ORDER BY occurred_at) rn

meaning: A payment that later fails or is refunded still shows its first status
impact: Target must choose SCD/latest-state semantics for payments (AUTO CDC)
risk: Porting as-is keeps wrong payment status; changing it alters history

recommendation.reason: payment lifecycle semantics need the payments owner (OQ-08)

name: Marketing consent requires consent on every order
logic: bool_and(marketing_consent) GROUP BY customer_id
plain: A customer counts as consenting only if every one of their orders carried consent
meaning: One order without consent removes the customer from marketing for good
impact: Port as-is into the Silver customer view; test with a mixed-consent customer
risk: Low; code and docs agree

name: Customer country is the alphabetically smallest
logic: min(country) GROUP BY customer_id
plain: If a customer ordered from several countries, the one first in alphabetical order is kept, not the latest
meaning: Customer country is effectively arbitrary for customers seen in several countries
impact: Decide latest / most frequent / billing country before building the target
risk: Residency or tax reporting by country could be wrong

recommendation.reason: looks unintended; needs a business owner (OQ-09)

name: PII pseudonymised as salted SHA-256 of the latest value
logic: sha256('{salt}:' || arg_max(email, occurred_at)); same for iban
plain: Email and IBAN in Silver are a salted hash of the customer's most recent value

evidence.excerpt: Why salted hash instead of format-preserving encryption?

meaning: Silver never holds clear email or IBAN, only a linkable hash
impact: Target keeps the same hash (salt from a secret scope) or moves to UC column masks
risk: A different salt in the target breaks joins to existing hashes

recommendation.reason: code and RFC agree; salt handling is a separate finding

name: Name is never hashed into Silver
logic: NULL as name_hash
plain: The customer name column in Silver is always empty
meaning: Names are not captured at all downstream of Bronze
impact: Drop the column in the target unless a use case needs it
risk: Low

recommendation.reason: read verbatim; harmless to keep as-is

name: Incremental load by event time, insert-only
logic: WHERE occurred_at > watermark; INSERT OR IGNORE INTO silver.orders
plain: Each run only picks events newer than the last processed event time and never updates existing rows

evidence.excerpt: INSERT OR IGNORE INTO silver.orders (order_id, customer_id, amount_eur, country, occurred_at, dedup_count)

conflicts.note: says the batch path re-reads the durable event log from earliest

meaning: Late events and corrections are dropped by the scheduled incremental run
impact: Target needs watermarks with lateness tolerance or AUTO CDC
risk: Gold silently differs from a full rebuild; reconciliation will flag gaps

recommendation.reason: docs and code disagree on full vs incremental (OQ-10)

name: Customers are derived from orders only
logic: ... FROM bronze.orders GROUP BY customer_id
plain: A customer exists only once they have placed an order; clicks and payments alone do not create one
meaning: Browsing-only visitors never become customers in reporting
impact: Keep the same grain in the target customer table
risk: Low

name: Bronze ignores repeated event ids
logic: INSERT OR IGNORE INTO bronze.orders ... (event_id PRIMARY KEY)
plain: A message delivered twice is stored once

evidence.excerpt: Batch append with `INSERT OR IGNORE` and deterministic `event_id` keys.

meaning: Duplicate deliveries from the bus do not double revenue
impact: Target Bronze needs the same idempotent key (MERGE on event_id or dropDuplicates)
risk: Low

name: Velocity alert: more than 5 payments in a 300 s window
logic: if stats.count == self._velocity_threshold + 1  (window from _window_key(ts), threshold 5, window 300 s)
plain: A customer making a 6th payment inside the same 5-minute window triggers one HIGH alert per window

conflicts.note: says rolling windows; README.md:215 says fixed buckets; paper says tumbling

meaning: Fraud bursts that straddle two windows are not flagged
impact: Target streaming job must pick tumbling vs sliding windows explicitly
risk: Different window type changes alert volumes and misses or adds fraud

recommendation.reason: three documents disagree on window type (OQ-11)

name: Amount z-score alert above 3 standard deviations
logic: len(history)>=3; std with n-1; abs(amount-mean)/std > 3.0; history excludes current, max 200
plain: A payment far above the customer's usual amounts (3 std) raises a MEDIUM alert once 3 prior payments exist

evidence.excerpt: if std > 0 and abs(payment.amount_eur - mean) / std > self._amount_zscore:
The current payment is excluded from the baseline

meaning: Unusually large payments per customer are flagged
impact: Port to a stateful stream with the same history size and threshold
risk: State held in memory; history size differences change alerts

name: Country mismatch alert
logic: if payment.country != payment.merchant_country -> GEO_MISMATCH, LOW
plain: A payment whose billing country differs from the merchant country raises a LOW alert

evidence.excerpt: | GEO_MISMATCH | billing country ≠ merchant country | LOW |

meaning: All cross-border purchases are flagged
impact: Port as a stateless filter
risk: Low

name: Fraud scorer drops payments of erased customers
logic: if self._suppression_check(payment.customer_id): incr('suppressed_for_erasure'); commit
plain: Once a customer asks for erasure, their new payments are no longer scored

evidence.excerpt: Add `customer_id` to the in-memory suppression set **and** the durable `governance.suppression_registry`

meaning: Erased customers stop producing fraud alerts
impact: Target stream must read the suppression table (or a row filter) continuously
risk: Fraud on an erased account goes unseen; a legal and fraud-policy trade-off

name: Customer 360 measures
logic: COUNT(DISTINCT order_id), COALESCE(SUM(amount_eur),0), COALESCE(AVG(amount_eur),0), COALESCE(fraud_flag,FALSE)
plain: Orders, total spend and average order value per customer in EUR; fraud flag is true if any alert of any severity exists
meaning: The headline customer metrics and a fraud flag that a single LOW alert switches on
impact: Define these once as UC metric views; agree fraud_flag severity
risk: A LOW geo alert marks a customer as fraud in the 360 view

recommendation.reason: fraud_flag severity needs the fraud owner (OQ-12)

name: Amounts treated as EUR; currency dropped
logic: silver.orders keeps amount_eur only; bronze.orders.currency not carried
plain: All amounts are assumed to already be in euros; the currency column is discarded

evidence.excerpt: INSERT OR IGNORE INTO silver.orders (order_id, customer_id, amount_eur, country, occurred_at, dedup_count)

meaning: Non-euro orders, if any exist, are summed as if they were euros
impact: Confirm all sources are EUR or add conversion in Silver
risk: Revenue overstated or understated for non-EUR markets

name: Erasure cascade: mask Bronze, delete Silver/Gold/alerts, re-export lake
logic: UPDATE bronze.* SET pii='<anonymized>'; DELETE silver.*, gold.*, bronze.fraud_alerts; on_complete -> export_lake
plain: On an erasure request, raw PII is overwritten, derived rows are deleted and the local lake files are rewritten

evidence.excerpt: "UPDATE bronze.orders SET email=?, iban=? WHERE customer_id=?",

conflicts.note: architecture lists fewer steps (no fraud_alerts, no lake re-export)

meaning: The documented six-step erasure is what the code runs on the local warehouse
impact: Target erasure job must cover the same stores plus Delta history (VACUUM)
risk: Stores outside the warehouse are not covered (see findings)

recommendation.reason: code matches the detailed erasure doc

name: Full rebuild ignores the suppression registry
logic: build_silver: DELETE FROM silver.customers; INSERT ... FROM bronze.orders GROUP BY customer_id (no suppression filter)
plain: Rebuilding Silver from Bronze brings erased customers back because their rows stay in Bronze with customer_id

conflicts.note: says persisting the suppression means the guarantee holds across restarts

meaning: An erased customer reappears in Silver and Gold after the next full rebuild
impact: Target must filter suppressed ids in every rebuild or delete Bronze rows
risk: Art. 17 breach recurring after each full refresh

name: Marketing consent defaults to false
logic: consent_default: bool = Field(default=False)
plain: When a source does not say, the customer is treated as not consenting

evidence.excerpt: consent_default: bool = Field(default=False, description="Default consent flag")

meaning: Opt-out by default; only explicit consent counts
impact: Carry as a pipeline default; record who may change it
risk: Low; safe default, but used only by the synthetic producer

name: Erasure SLA is 60 s from request time
logic: latency = completed_at - requested_at; if latency > sla: incr('erasure_sla_breach')
plain: An erasure must finish within 60 seconds of the request, queue time included, or a breach is counted
meaning: The internal target for completing an erasure
impact: A Delta-based erasure job must be sized to meet it, or the SLA renegotiated
risk: Serverless job start-up alone may exceed 60 s

name: PII column classification by 60% majority
logic: classify_column(..., threshold=0.6): tag if n/total >= threshold
plain: A column is treated as PII when at least 60% of sampled values look like email, IBAN, IP, phone or name

evidence.excerpt: def classify_column(name: str, sample_values: list[str], threshold: float = 0.6) -> list[str]:
60%). A column only gets a PII tag when most of its samples agree

meaning: How the pipeline decides a new column holds personal data
impact: Replace with UC data classification or keep as an expectation
risk: Heuristics give false positives that stop the pipeline

name: Failed quality check stops the run
logic: if failed: raise RuntimeError('data quality gate failed: ...')
plain: If any data-quality check fails, the lake export does not happen

evidence.excerpt: | Data quality | all checks pass | DAG aborts if any gate fails |

meaning: Bad data is not published
impact: Map to Lakeflow expectations with FAIL UPDATE where needed
risk: Low

name: Consent quality check compares a column with its own copy
logic: SELECT count(*) FROM gold.customer_360 WHERE consents_marketing <> marketing_consent
plain: The consent check can never fail, because both columns are written from the same value

evidence.excerpt: "SELECT count(*) c FROM gold.customer_360 WHERE consents_marketing <> marketing_consent"

conflicts.note: says consent_gating ensures no non-consenting customers in the marketing view

meaning: No check actually prevents non-consenting customers reaching marketing data
impact: Build a real consent filter (view or row filter) and a test for it
risk: Marketing could use customers without consent (Art. 6/7)

recommendation.reason: read verbatim; gold build writes both columns from c.marketing_consent

name: Dashboard stats fall back to the public dataset
logic: if stats['total_rows'] == 0: read hf://datasets/swadhinbiswas/eustream/*.parquet
plain: When the warehouse is empty the overview shows counts from the public Hugging Face copy instead
meaning: Users can see numbers from a different system without being told
impact: Drop the fallback; target dashboard reads one governed source
risk: Decisions made on stale or foreign numbers

name: Malformed or unexpected events are skipped silently
logic: except Exception: continue  (bronze load); incr('malformed_events'); commit (stream)
plain: Events that fail to parse are dropped without a dead-letter copy
meaning: Bad source data disappears without trace
impact: Target Bronze keeps a rescued-data column or quarantine table
risk: Undetected data loss and unreconcilable counts
